title: Targeting BACH1 by HPPE inhibits the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway and malignant phenotype in glioblastoma cells.
authors: Wang, Yuzhu; Yang, Changxiao; Guo, Li; Nie, Peiyu; Hu, Xiaowei; Zhou, Hongfeng; Li, Huibo; Tao, Haiquan; Wu, Jin
journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子HPPE靶向BACH1抑制胶质母细胞瘤Wnt通路，涉及BACH1与TCF-4的蛋白-DNA相关互作及分子动力学/对接模拟，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合，方法可迁移但对象偏离。
abstract: BTB domain and CNC homology 1 (BACH1) has been reported to be a vital regulator of tumor progression. However, methods for targeting BACH1 in cancers have not been fully researched. In this study, we identified BACH1 as a poor prognosis-related factor in patients with GBM. Furthermore, a small-molecule compound, HPPE, was found to interact with BACH1 and inhibit the progression of GBM in vitro and in vivo. Molecular dynamics analysis, molecular docking simulation, MST assay, and co-IP experiments revealed that HPPE principally binds to BACH1 at the bZIP domain on the C-terminus and promotes the competitive binding of BACH1 and TCF-4, thus inhibiting formation of the beta-catenin/TCF-4 complex. HPPE incubation inhibited proliferation, promoted apoptosis, and induced G2/M arrest, indicating a potential synergistic effect with temozolomide in GBM cells. RNA-seq, qRT‒PCR, and gene enrichment analyses revealed that the induction of HPPE repressed the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway. Further experiments revealed that BTB domain deletion from BACH1 eliminated its ability to interact with TCF-4 and significantly rescued the inhibition of Wnt/beta-catenin signaling and the reduction of malignant phenotype induced by HPPE in GBM cells. In vivo experiments revealed that HPPE prolonged the survival time of mice, inhibited Wnt/beta-catenin pathway activity and had a synergistic effect with TMZ in a xenograft model. In summary, these findings provide potential combined therapeutic strategies for glioma by targeting the C-terminus of BACH1 and inhibiting the activation of WNT signaling.
abstract_zh: BTB结构域和CNC同源蛋白1（BACH1）已被报道为肿瘤进展的关键调控因子。然而，在癌症中靶向BACH1的方法尚未得到充分研究。在本研究中，我们确定BACH1是胶质母细胞瘤（GBM）患者中与不良预后相关的因子。此外，发现小分子化合物HPPE能与BACH1相互作用，并在体外和体内抑制GBM的进展。分子动力学分析、分子对接模拟、微量热泳动（MST）实验和共免疫沉淀（co-IP）实验揭示，HPPE主要结合BACH1 C末端的bZIP结构域，并促进BACH1与TCF-4的竞争性结合，从而抑制β-catenin/TCF-4复合物的形成。HPPE孵育抑制增殖、促进凋亡并诱导G2/M期阻滞，表明其在GBM细胞中与替莫唑胺具有潜在协同效应。RNA-seq、qRT-PCR和基因富集分析显示，HPPE的诱导抑制了Wnt/β-catenin通路。进一步实验揭示，BACH1中BTB结构域的缺失消除了其与TCF-4相互作用的能力，并显著逆转了HPPE在GBM细胞中诱导的Wnt/β-catenin信号抑制和恶性表型减少。体内实验显示，HPPE延长了小鼠的生存时间，抑制了Wnt/β-catenin通路活性，并在异种移植模型中与TMZ具有协同效应。总之，这些发现通过靶向BACH1的C末端并抑制WNT信号激活，为胶质瘤提供了潜在的联合治疗策略。
